findings: Actor+344 is motion state; actor BDX context is the QWORD at+1456. Do not equate the animation clock with AI.
Descriptor+8 is normally one-time initialization: it runs until Actor+2488 bit0x80 is set. Three YS enemy-family prefixes and their preparation callbacks confirm the branch meaning.
Four native stop IDs share an aggregate mask. Duration0 is indefinite. ID1 is already used by native gameplay; removal by ID cannot prove trainer ownership.
Existing extracted baseline00battle.bin has15 sorted stop rows and only masks1,3,7. The loaded table and modifications must be checked separately.
Stop mask bit0 suppresses core actor update, while motion pose/attached effects and outer dispatcher work can continue. VM has multiple direct and synchronous callers.
The developer menu's 'stop enemy' label is a UI label, not sufficient proof its configuration bit has a gameplay consumer.

potential_controls.idea: Selected enemy stop with a native stop row
potential_controls.remaining: Fresh actor/status/scene membership lease; all four IDs must map to valid rows and a free slot must exist; native ID ownership conflicts unresolved. Must preserve unrelated stop entries and timers. No invented stop ID or blanket removal.
Need exact caller/descriptor routes for ordinary enemy and boss VM execution, immediate-event paths, and action handlers; animation freeze alone is insufficient.
